hed: EPA set to announce final repeal of Biden power-plant carbon limits at Houston G20
dek: The Environmental Protection Agency is set Monday to announce a final rule repealing the Biden administration’s greenhouse-gas emission limits on coal- and natural-gas-fired power plants, Reuters reported, with the rollout planned on the sidelines of a G20 energy ministers’ meeting in Houston. The 2024 standards would have required carbon-capture or retirement pathways for covered plants and were projected to cut about 1 billion metric tons of greenhouse gases by 2047; the Trump EPA argues the rules raised costs and threatened reliability. Administrator Lee Zeldin has cast the move as part of a broader deregulatory push, and environmental groups say they will sue.

cl.body: Reuters’ Monday exclusive, the AP/ABC wire, and the Center for Biological Diversity’s Maggie Coulter cast the Houston finalization as erasing a core climate tool for a sector that accounts for nearly a quarter of U.S. greenhouse gases — Coulter called denying that pollution “utterly reckless” and warned of more heat, storms, and wildfire harm — while advocacy groups argue the repeal will raise health costs in fenceline communities and face immediate court challenges.

cr.body: Zeldin’s deregulatory framing, the Washington Examiner’s power-plant write-through, and National Rural Electric Cooperative Association CEO Jim Matheson’s Utility Dive remarks cast the repeal as restoring baseload capacity and cutting compliance costs — Zeldin has said Biden-era carbon rules were designed to “suffocate” coal and that families need reliable, affordable power, while co-ops call the 40% capacity threshold and 90% capture mandate untenable amid data-center load growth.
